title: Quiet the workerd stderr noise in a green vitest run
description:
A fully GREEN vitest run in cloudflare/ emits a wall of workerd stderr: 'evicted mid-commit', 'Engine was never started', "Worker's code had hung". Found by tick ncr (Biome), which lost time distinguishing 'hung' from 'slow' while reading it.

These look like deliberate negative-path scenarios leaking their noise rather than real faults — the suite passes. The cost is not correctness, it is READABILITY OF A FAILURE: a CI log where a green run already prints alarming stderr is a log where a real failure does not stand out. That is the same class as the five load-sensitive tests in cy2 — a signal that cries wolf stops being read.

Work:
- Identify which tests produce each message, and confirm each is an intended negative path.
- Suppress or capture the expected stderr at its source (vitest onConsoleLog / per-test capture), NOT globally — a genuinely unexpected workerd message must still reach the log.
- Prove it: a green run is quiet, and an injected real fault still prints.

Run: cd cloudflare && pnpm exec vitest run
acceptance_criteria: A fully passing vitest run emits no workerd stderr; an injected genuine workerd fault still surfaces its message in the output
